summary: The root QBR refers to a type of small bird, specifically a lark. It is known by several similar-sounding names, such as qubbar, qubbarah, and qunbura. The plural form is qanabir.
lane: قُبَّرٌ ذ (S, Msb, K) and (K) and (S, K) and , this last occurring in a Rejez, to be cited below, (S,) The [ lark; ] a kind of bird, (S, K,) resembling the حُمَّرَة ; (TA;) a kind of small bird; (Msb:) n. un. قُبَّرَةٌ (S, Msb, K) and قُبَرَةٌ (K) and قُنْبُرَةٌ , (S, Msb,) which last is the form used by the vulgar, (S,) or it is not allowable, or it is a form of weak authority, (K,) and is also pronounced قُنْبَرَةٌ : (Msb:) pl. of قنبراء , (S, K,) and of قنبرة , (Msb,) قَنَابِرُ . headwords.gloss: He buried; concealed it in the earth
headwords.def: قَبَرَ , aor. قَبُرَ and قَبِرَ , inf. n. قَبْرٌ (S, Msb, K) and مَقْبَرٌ , (K,) He buried a corpse; (S, Msb, K:) concealed it in the earth. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: He made him to be buried; He ordered that he should be buried; He permitted that he should be buried

headwords.def: اقبرهُ He made him to be buried: so in the Kur, lxxx. 21: (Fr, S:) where it is meant that man is not made by God to be thrown, when dead, to the dogs, (S,) or to the birds and wild beasts. (Fr.) He ordered that he should be buried. (S, Mgh, Msb.) [ He permitted that he should be buried. ] The tribe of Temeem said to El-Hejjáj, who had slain Sálih the son of 'Abder-Rahmán, أَقْبِرْنَا صَالِحًا , meaning, Permit us to bury Sálih. (S, * TA.) You say also اقبر القَوْمَ , meaning, He gave them their slain that they might burg him. (K.) He assigned to him, or made for him, a grave (ISk, S, Msb, K) to be buried in it: (S:) he made him to have a grave. (Mgh.) Accord. to some, He ordered him to dig a grave. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: A grave, tomb, sepulchre; place of burial
headwords.def: قَبْرٌ A grave, tomb, sepulchre, or place of burial, of a human being: (K:) pl. قُبُور . (S, Msb, K.)
